overall_quality.reason: Accurate, relevant explanation of sequential vs parallel processing and self-attention, but lacks depth on positional encoding and training/inference distinctions.
overall_quality.evidence: Transformers and RNNs both handle sequences, but they do so in fundamentally different ways. RNNs process sequences in a sequential manner, one element at a time, which can be slow and inefficient for long sequences. Transformers, on the other hand, use a parallel approach, allowing them to handle sequences much more efficiently. They achieve this by using self-attention mechanisms that allow each part of the sequence to interact with every other part in parallel. This makes transformers particularly well-suited for tasks like language modeling and machine translation.
